text:
rachel: quick sync thread - proposing a runtime soft-quota shim so the router can apply tenant budget-aware routing without changing the policy DSL. idea: emit backpressure hints (soft_quota_exhausted:true) per-tenant + per-route weight adjustments instead of hard rejects.
omar: how is this different from the preemptive-slot model we already have?
rachel: preemptive slots allocate capacity and can evict lower-priority requests. soft-quota is advisory: we still let requests through but bias routing toward cheaper / lower-latency variants and reduce hedging for the tenant once their spend hits a soft threshold. avoids hard rejects and sudden customer errors.
kai: what signals drive soft thresholds? raw token spend? cost-weighted tokens? rolling window?
rachel: default = cost-weighted tokens over a rolling 1h window. window and thresholds configurable per-tenant. also support region-scoped quotas (e.g., EU vs US).
neha: concern: tenants might game this by moving traffic to cheaper models and cause unfair load shifts across infra.
rachel: mitigations: 1) global fairness clamp that limits percent of traffic that can be rerouted per-tenant per-region; 2) cooldown windows after an adjustment to prevent oscillation; 3) optional tenant opt-in for aggressive moves.
omar: policy engine implications - DSL authors might want to inspect runtime hints. do we expose anything into the DSL?achel: initial plan: no DSL changes. instead expose a runtime API for read-only hints (for observability) and a tiny runtime function if needed later, e.g. runtime_hint("soft_quota"). prefer keeping DSL stable.
pat: ops questions - surface to oncall: we need alerts for large route shifts and cost deltas. propose alerts: >10% reroute for top-50 routes in 10m OR >5% cost delta for tenant in 1h.
ops-bot: created alert template soft-quota-route-shift channels=#eng-oncall,#eng-sre severity=medium
kai: metrics to instrument: 1h spend per tenant (cost-weighted), rerouted percent traffic, hedge-suppression rate, p99 latency delta, fairness-clamp hits, rollback count.
neha: rollout plan?
rachel: staged rollout: 1) sim-only mode inside routing-sim for 2 weeks to validate behavior; 2) dry-run in prod where router logs hints but makes no decision for 1 week; 3) advisory adjustments at 1% traffic (small sample) for 3 days; 4) ramp to 25% with monitoring; 5) evaluate fairness and telemetry, then 50%+ if healthy. opt-in tenants can be migrated first.
omar: storage and algorithm: keep a bounded rolling window counter. prefer fixed-ring buckets (e.g., 60 x 1m buckets for 1h) to keep memory predictable. use cost-weighted increments when requests complete.
pat: ops playbook: toggle feature.soft_quota_runtime, a single boolean to enable advice path; fallback is to disable and return to preemptive slots behavior. also provide script to recompute historical cost-weighted tokens for tenants for debugging.
kai: question: should the router bias model selection directly or hand off a hint to matchmaker?
rachel: propose router applies lightweight scoring bias (cheap weight delta) and also emits a hint to matchmaker. matchmaker makes final decision. add flag soft_quota_matchmaker_influence=0.2 default so matchmaker uses it as soft input.
neha: test plan: inject synthetic tenants with spike patterns and assert no tenant can cause >20% reroute impact on others. property test for oscillation with cooldowns; fuzz test on window sizes and thresholds.
rachel: dedicated-capacity tenants: soft-quota should not affect them unless tenant policy explicitly allows it. add opt-out flag per-tenant.
pat: telemetry: dual-write old preemptive metrics and new advisory metrics for 4 weeks to compare. add canary evals for quality impact on top 100 routes.
omar: owners: runtime/router = @kai, policy/compiler = @omar, ops/telemetry = @pat. i'll own rollout docs and coordination.
kai: rough timeline: spec and sim harness changes 2w, runtime impl 3w, dry-run + canary week 4, ramp across 6-8w.
neha: open questions: how do we represent the hint in traces? propose span tag soft_quota={status, window_cost, clamp_applied}.
rachel: good. final open Q: fairness clamp default value. suggest 10% per-tenant per-region, but put it in RFC for bikeshedding.
pat: lets sync Thurs 10am to finalize rollout doc and alerts. thanks all.
